text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: gateway-prod us-east-1 — elevated 5xx rate (504 spike). 4.1% of requests in the last 5m. Sampled errors show timeouts hitting gateway->upstream. No automatic mitigation triggered.

matt_oncall: Oncall here, ack. I'm pulling logs now. Any customer-facing impact seen yet? :eyes:

maya_support: seeing several new support tickets complaining about request timeouts — customer Acorn Health and BetaPayments called in. Tickets linked: https://support.redwood/email/INC-3421, https://support.redwood/email/INC-3422

jordan_sre: quick triage — grep of edge proxy logs shows a large cluster of KV cache misses followed by upstream 504s. Also seeing lots of requests without x-request-id header which is preventing trace correlation. Log query: Logs -> gw-prod (us-east) query: `status:504 and message: "kvcache miss" | count()`

leah_eng: we shipped a routing change 2 hours ago that increased keyspace sharding of the cache — could be related. Rollout was incremental but maybe a bad shard placement. Rolling back is high risk while traffic is live.

alex_prod: if the kvcache miss is spiking upstream latency, we can do a short-term fallback: route traffic to the previous routing-policy for the next 20m (circuit-breaker style) and enable extra retries at the edge. That should reduce 504s quickly.

matt_oncall: Jordan, can you surface the missing trace/span ids? We need at least one quick instrumentation so we can follow errors end-to-end.

jordan_sre: yep — traces show spanid missing in ~60% of error requests. I'm going to enable edge debug-headers and increase trace sampling for gw-prod for 10m. Patch I'm about to run:

```
# enable debug logging and 100% trace sampling for gw-prod
kubectl -n proxy patch configmap gateway-config --type merge -p '{"data":{"debug.logging":"true","trace.sampling":"1.0"}}'
```

jordan_sre: Also injecting x-request-id when absent in the proxy for a 15-minute window with this hotpatch (non-disruptive):

```
# hotpatch edge to inject request-id header
kubectl -n proxy rollout restart deployment/gw-edge
# (hotpatch applies middleware rule to set header if missing)
```

deploy-bot: deploy started: gateway-config patch by jordan_sre @ 1758005850

deploy-bot: deploy succeeded: gateway-config patch completed @ 1758005923 :white_check_mark:

jordan_sre: instrumented logs now include kvcache key + request-id for affected requests. Example debug log snippet:

```
[2026-02-14T21:17:30Z] proxy=gw-edge shard=42 kvcache=miss key="user_session:abc123" upstream.latency_ms=1200 set_reqid=1 req_id=rid_5f8a
```

maya_support: starting customer comms. Leah, can you confirm likely ETA for route fallback if needed? I want to tell Acorn Health if we expect mitigation in ~15-30m.

leah_eng: If we opt for traffic fallback it's a config flip in routing policy that takes ~90s to propagate. I can do it on your go. But let's watch the debug logs for 10m and confirm kvcache hitrate change first.

alex_prod: Also adding temporary retry at edge (2 retries, 100ms backoff) to reduce upstream 504 surface area. Command I had ready:

```
# edge config snippet (temporary)
retries:
  attempts: 2
  per_try_timeout: 100ms
```

matt_oncall: go ahead and apply retries now. Leah, if hitrate doesn't improve in 10m, do fallback.

leah_eng: applying retries now. Will monitor.

jordan_sre: note — we still have ~2% of requests without traces even after injection; I'll add a lightweight secondary sampler that tags logs with req_id so we can stitch in logs if spans are absent.

alex_prod: +1 on sampler. Also recommend adding a lightweight metric that counts errors with kvcache miss to the incident dashboard so PM/CS can track customer impact real-time.

matt_oncall: created incident dashboard and added Acorn Health and BetaPayments as watched customers. Dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood/dashboard/incident-1758004321

maya_support: sent interim update to impacted customers: "We're seeing intermittent request timeouts in us-east-1; engineering has applied additional tracing and retries while we investigate. We'll update in 30 minutes." (sent @ 1758007000)

jordan_sre: After retries and request-id injection we're seeing 504 rate drop from 4.1% to 1.2% in ~8m. kvcache miss rate still elevated but trending down. Logs show many keys getting repopulated.

matt_oncall: nice. keep watching. Jordan, leave debug-logging on for another 10m then revert to normal to avoid noise.

jordan_sre: Will revert at 1758011521 (10m). Reversion command queued.

deploy-bot: reversion deploy started @ 1758011521

deploy-bot: reversion deploy succeeded @ 1758011583 :white_check_mark:

jordan_sre: debug logs reverted. Final numbers: 504 rate stabilized at 0.4%, kvcache miss rate decreased 70% vs peak. We captured traces for ~92% of previous error requests; attached sample traces to the incident timeline.

maya_support: updated customers — told them root cause investigation and that engineering is doing follow-up patch to routing shard placement. Customers acknowledged; no immediate SLA escalations.

leah_eng: follow-up action: revert the problematic shard placement in the routing rollout (non-emergency), add post-deploy smoke tests that validate cache hitrates per shard. I'll own the rollout revert and tests.

matt_oncall: preparing handoff to night oncall. Summary for next oncall @frank_oncall: short-lived kvcache shard placement issue caused gateway 504 spike. Mitigation: request-id injection, edge retries, temporary routing fallback ready (not applied). Observability fixes: temporary debug logging, sampler, metrics added. Current status: stable. Next steps: Leah will revert routing change and add tests. Jordan to attach traces to timeline. Support updated customers.

matt_oncall: frank_oncall you have the incident. Key artifacts: dashboard https://grafana.redwood/dashboard/incident-1758004321, logs query https://logs.redwood/q/1758004321, traces attached in incident doc. Ping me if anything degrades. :thumbsup:

frank_oncall: ack, taking over. Thanks all. I'll monitor until escalation window ends. :eyes:
